## Important dates

Applications through Mon Master: The dates for the 2027 application process are not public yet. The application period should typically start around February 2027.

Applications through Études en France: Applications should be sent from October to December 2026, to apply for the 2027-2028 academic year. Please contact your local Campus France office to know the specific deadlines that apply yo you (see the list of Campus France offices here).

## How to apply?

The application process depends on your nationality, the country in which you are currently living, and whether you apply as a full-time student or through the Erasmus programme.

### French / EU students [...] Important note: You may find two distinct pages on Études en France for the Master in Data science: one to apply to University of Lille, the other to apply to Centrale Lille. While this is the same Master program, you must apply through University of Lille only (not Centrale Lille), otherwise your application will not be processed.

If you do not qualify for the Études en France procedure, you must follow the same application procedure as French/EU students (please see above).

### Erasmus students

If you want to attend classes in the Master through the Erasmus programme, you should follow the Erasmus procedure of your home university and list courses of the Master in your learning agreement. The adminitrative staff of your university will send us your application file directly. [...] ### French / EU students

French and EU students, as well as students currently living in France or the EU (regardless of their nationalities), must apply through the national platform: Mon Master. Please note that the Master in Data science is referenced twice on MonMaster: under Université de Lille, and under Centrale Lille; you must apply through the page of Université de Lille only.

### Foreign students (outside of the EU)

If you are currently enrolled in a higher education institution in France or in the EU, you must use the same procedure as French / EU students (please see above).
results.raw_content: Formations en Informatique de Lille Portail pédagogique [![accueil FIL](css/trans.gif)](https://portail.fil.univ-lille.fr "FIL") [L1 Maths-Info](index.php?dipl=L1_MI) [Licence Info](index.php?dipl=L) [Master Info](index.php?dipl=MInfo) [Master Miage](index.php?dipl=MMiage) [Master BioInfo](index.php?dipl=M1MISO) [Master DS](index.php?dipl=MDS) [Alternance](index.php?dipl=Alternance) [General Information](index.php?dipl=MDS&sem=MDSinfo&ue=ACCUEIL) [M1](index.php?dipl=MDS&sem=M1DS&ue=ACCUEIL) [M2](index.php?dipl=MDS&sem=M2DS&ue=ACCUEIL) Vous êtes ici : [FIL](https://sciences-technologies.univ-lille.fr/informatique/) > [Portail](index.php) > [Master DS](index.php?dipl=MDS) > [M1](index.php?dipl=MDS&sem=M1DS&ue=ACCUEIL) [Presentation](#) [Applying](#) [Courses](#) [Internship](#) ## Aims of the first year of the Master The major goal of the first year of the Master is to provide students with: * the scientific background required to master machine learning at a high level: mathematics (calculus, algebra, optimization, probabilities, statistics), computer science (algorithms, analysis of algorithms, databases), signal processing, * the fundamentals of machine learning: supervised and unsupervised machine learning models, evaluation of machine learning models, neural networks, decision theory, etc. The first year of the master mixes up theory and practice. Each course offers both theoretical lectures and exercise or lab sessions where students learn how to apply the theoretical content of the lectures in practice. The practice of machine learning is emphasized through a one-week data challenge and a final internship in a company or an academic lab. In their first year, students are also initiated to research in machine learning through regular seminars given by researchers and practitioners in the field, and through a research project spread over 5 months in one of the research labs of University of Lille, Centrale Lille, or IMT Nord Europe. ## Who can apply? The M1 in data science is open to students who have completed (or will have completed by the end of the academic year) a Bachelor / Licence (or an equivalent degree) in one of the following fields: * Pure or applied mathematics, * Computer science, * Mathematics and computer science, * Mathematics and computer science applied to social science (French MIASHS programme), * Electrical engineering, * Computer engineering, * or any other Bachelor degree with a strong curriculum in maths and computer science. Students who are currently enrolled in post-graduate studies (Master programme or Engineering school) can still apply as long as they hold a Bachelor in one of the aforementioned fields. Applicants must demonstrate proficiency in English at the CEFR level B2 or above. Your level in English can be demonstrated in several ways: by an official certificate (TOEIC, TOEFL, IELTS, etc.) or through a statement issued by your university indicating your level on the CEFR scale (B2, C1, etc.). ## Important dates **Applications through Mon Master:** The dates for the 2027 application process are not public yet. The application period should typically start around February 2027. **Applications through Études en France:** Applications should be sent from October to December 2026, to apply for the 2027-2028 academic year. Please contact your local Campus France office to know the specific deadlines that apply yo you (see the list of Campus France offices [here](https://www.campusfrance.org/en/espaces)). ## How to apply? The application process depends on your nationality, the country in which you are currently living, and whether you apply as a full-time student or through the Erasmus programme. ### French / EU students French and EU students, as well as students currently living in France or the EU (regardless of their nationalities), must apply through the national platform: [Mon Master](https://www.monmaster.gouv.fr/master/universite-de-lille-epe/science-des-donnees-1?q=data%20science%20lille&position=0&layout=1). Please note that the Master in Data science is referenced twice on MonMaster: under Université de Lille, and under Centrale Lille; you must apply through the [page of Université de Lille](https://www.monmaster.gouv.fr/master/universite-de-lille-epe/science-des-donnees-1?q=data%20science%20lille&position=0&layout=1) only. ### Foreign students (outside of the EU) If you are currently enrolled in a higher education institution in France or in the EU, you must use the same procedure as French / EU students (please see above). If you are currently living in one of the countries listed under the Campus France procedure [Études en France](https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/etudesenfrance/), you must follow the specific procedure of Campus France. Please refer to the [Études en France website](https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/etudesenfrance/) to check if you qualify for their procedure and access the detailed application process. Please note that the Études en France process starts very early on: the process to join the Master at year N typically starts during the first semester (usually in October) of the year N-1. **Important note:** You may find two distinct pages on Études en France for the Master in Data science: one to apply to University of Lille, the other to apply to Centrale Lille. While this is the same Master program, **you must apply through University of Lille only** (not Centrale Lille), otherwise your application will not be processed. If you do not qualify for the Études en France procedure, you must follow the same application procedure as French/EU students (please see above). ### Erasmus students If you want to attend classes in the Master through the Erasmus programme, you should follow the Erasmus procedure of your home university and list courses of the Master in your learning agreement. The adminitrative staff of your university will send us your application file directly. ## What documents should I provide to apply? Applicants must provide the following documents with their application: * A curriculum vitae * Transcripts of grades of your current and previous higher education programmes * A cover letter (lettre de motivation) * One or several documents attesting your level in English Additional documents may be required depending on the procedure through which you are applying. Optionally, applicants can provide some of the following documents: * Recommandation letters * Official certificate of proficiency in English (TOEIC, TOEFL, IELTS, etc.) * Statement of proficiency in English issued by your university ## M1: 1st year, 1st (fall / M1S1) semester and 2nd (spring / M1S2) semester All courses take place over 24 hours. Two refresher courses are proposed in computer science and mathematics to help students who would need some upgrade to attend the program in good conditions; taking at least one of them is mandatory and decided by the teaching team based on the student's background. Students can always choose to attend both. A complete description of all courses of the first year (M1) is available [here](https://nextcloud.univ-lille.fr/index.php/s/dtoSkMp9kbQ7GBj/download). ### Courses of the first (fall) semester | Name | Status | Teaching hours | Credits (ECTS) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Refresher in mathematics | Optional | 24 | 3 | | Refresher in computer science | Optional | 24 | | Python and tools for research | Mandatory | 24 | | Fundamental notions of mathematics | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Probability 1 | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Statistics 1 | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Algorithms and their complexity 1 | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Data bases 1 | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Machine learning 1: Hands on! | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Machine learning 2: The landscape of machine learning | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Ethics & law: Legal aspects of data analysis | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | English | Optional | 24 | 3 | | Foreign language (other than English) | Optional | 24 | | French for foreign students | Optional | 24 | ### Courses of the second (spring) semester | Name | Status | Teaching hours | Credits (ECTS) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Probability 2: Markov chains & processes | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Statistics 2: Introduction to estimation | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Optimization and numerical analysis | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Algorithms & their complexity 2 | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Machine learning 3: Deep learning | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Models for machine learning | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Signal processing & functional data analysis | Mandatory | 24 | 3 | | Data challenge | Mandatory | 1 week | 3 | | Research project | Mandatory | 3 | | Seminars | Mandatory | | Internship | Mandatory | 6+ weeks | 3 | ## First year internship ### General information The internship of the first year is mandatory and must last at least 6 weeks. The typical duration is three to four months. It can be done in an academic lab of a company, in France or in a Foreign country. The topic of the internship must be related to the field of data science, in a broad sense. Eligible topics include: * Design, deployement, or experimental validation of machine learning models * Software development related to data management, data analysis, or machine learning * Database design, management, or * Mathematical modeling At the end of the internship, students must validate the internship through a memoir and a defense. ### Funding during the internship Under French regulations, the employer must provide a compensation to interns if the duration of the internship is 2 months or more. The minimum rate for the compensation is 4.05€/hour; many companies offer more. Students doing their internship abroad can apply for a mobility grant from the Graduate programme IKS or the Sherlock IA chair. The amount of the grant depends on the conditions of the internship. Calls for applications are sent to the students during the academic year. ### Examples of M1 Internships * Cloud shadow removal in sun observations, LIS, University of Toulon (Toulon, France) * Information extraction from legal documents, Lexis Nexis (Paris, France) * Implementation and assessment of function secret sharing algorithms, INRIA (Lille, France) * 3D detection of vulnerable road users, IMT Nord Europe (Lille, France)

results.raw_content: [Back to Search Programs](/search) # Master Informatique — E-services [Université de Lille](/university/universite-de-lille) Ronchin, France2 yearsTaught in FrenchOpen to international students ## About Master Informatique — E-services At Université de Lille, tuition comes to 250 EUR per year. E-services is a specialization within the Master Informatique at Université de Lille, in Villeneuve D'Ascq, France. This track within computer science focuses on the design, development, and delivery of digital services over networks, covering subjects such as web application development, service-oriented architecture, distributed systems, and the technologies used to build and operate online services accessed by users and other systems. Students typically study programming, web technologies, software architecture, and the methods used to design services that are reliable, secure, and able to scale to many users. Graduates from this kind of program commonly move into roles such as web developer, software engineer specializing in service-based architectures, IT consultant, or positions within companies that build and operate digital platforms and online services. The broad coverage of service design and web technology also supports careers in sectors where digital service delivery is central, including e-commerce, telecommunications, and public digital services. The program spans two years and leads to a master's degree, taught in French, so applicants should have a solid command of the language for technical and programming-focused coursework. The academic year begins in September. Yearly tuition is 250 EUR, in line with fees at French public universities. Students interested in building and operating digital services accessed over networks may find this specialization at Université de Lille a relevant route into that area of software development.
